intro: Picture this: you wake up in a small house ringed by green trees, the air cool and easy, birdsong instead of traffic — and a few minutes' drive later you're at Kung Wiman Beach, the east-coast shore known for clear water and a pretty coastal road. Forest Hill Resort is a small garden villa resort in the Kung Wiman Beach area of Na Yai Am, Chanthaburi, built around quiet and nature · it has several house types, from deluxe rooms and family rooms to villas with private pools and a house for groups of 8 · breakfast is included, parking is free, and pets are welcome · rates start at around THB 1,500/night, and the score from real reviews sits in good territory, around 9.

body.html: Forest Hill Resort overview — who it suits — To put it as briefly as possible, Forest Hill Resort is a small garden villa resort for people who want to escape the noise and stay surrounded by nature, somewhere quiet in the Kung Wiman Beach area of Na Yai Am, Chanthaburi · it isn't a big beachfront hotel with a fancy lobby and an infinity pool overlooking the sea, but a garden-house style stay, with several houses spread across grounds ringed by trees, giving a private and calm feel · what makes a lot of people choose this place is that some villas have their own private pool, plus larger houses that fit groups or families of up to 8, at prices more reachable than the pool villas in the main tourist towns · real reviews line up on this: the people it suits best are families travelling in numbers, groups of friends who want to rent a whole house, couples after some privacy, and people bringing pets along, since the resort welcomes pets (extra charge), which isn't common at seaside resorts · on the flip side, if you're after a stay right on the beach where you can walk straight down to the water, or you want a full set of big-hotel facilities, this may not be your answer, because its selling points are quiet, privacy, and being close to nature rather than luxury · the resort is still operating and is listed for booking on Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com, and Traveloka.

Location and getting there — Forest Hill Resort sits in Sanam Chai subdistrict, Na Yai Am, Chanthaburi, in the Kung Wiman Beach area, an east-coast shore that people from Bangkok and the eastern region like to visit on holidays · the strong point of the location is that it's only about 1–1.6 km from Kung Wiman Beach, just a few minutes' drive, which is handy if you want to head out for a stroll by the sea or catch the sunset, while the resort itself sits further back on the garden side, so it keeps a quiet feel with no wave noise or crowds of tourists · access is easy via Highway 4036, the coastal road with pretty views the whole way · around this area there are several interesting spots, including the Kung Wiman rock viewpoint nearby, the well-known Wat Khao Sukim, and not far off is the town of Chanthaburi with the Chanthaboon Riverside Community and the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception · one important note: this is a quiet out-of-town resort, so having your own car makes getting around easiest, because public transport in this area isn't as easy to flag down as in a big city · anyone without a car should plan their travel ahead.

"Very quiet place, surrounded by trees, fresh air, just a few minutes' drive to Kung Wiman Beach. Great for a stay where you don't have to rush, and the staff were kind and even recommended places to visit."

Room and house types — Forest Hill Resort is a small resort with houses spread across several buildings, not rows of rooms in a block like a hotel · from the available information, the houses come in several types to choose from by group size and budget · it starts with deluxe rooms for couples or two guests, with a quiet garden-house feel · stepping up to family rooms, some of which come with a small private pool · and the highlight many people are interested in is the villas with private pools, in several sizes, from a 3-bedroom queen layout sleeping 6 up to a house for 8 with 4 queen beds, ideal for groups of friends or large families who want to rent a whole house and stay together · in terms of in-room amenities, reviews and the property info note air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, free drinking water, and a kettle, all in line with standard leisure-stay expectations · what reviews agree on is that the rooms are clean and the garden-house atmosphere makes you feel relaxed · since it's a small place with a limited number of houses, rooms tend to fill quickly over long holidays, so booking ahead and asking clearly about the room type you want from the start is worth doing, especially if you're coming specifically for a villa with a private pool.

Facilities and the pool — Even though it's a small resort, Forest Hill Resort still has the basic facilities covered for a relaxing stay · there's a shared outdoor pool you can swim in amid the green garden setting, and for anyone who books a villa with a private pool, you get your own pool right at the house, which feels very private, especially for groups who don't want to share a pool with others · on top of that there's the resort restaurant, a small mini-mart, a BBQ grilling area, a relaxation garden, and a picnic corner · what's convenient for people driving themselves is the free parking on the resort grounds, plus valet service · free Wi-Fi in the common areas, and a 24-hour front desk · what sets Forest Hill apart from the usual stay is its pet policy, which allows you to bring dogs and cats along (extra charge), a plus that pet owners look for, since most seaside resorts don't accept them · to be honest, the facilities here aren't 4–5 star resort luxury — there's no fitness centre or full spa — but for a simple, relaxing stay in nature, it's pitched well for the price.

Food and breakfast — Forest Hill Resort has its own resort restaurant, and breakfast is included in the room rate, which helps you start the day without heading out to find somewhere in the morning · real reviews speak positively about the resort's food, saying the food quality is good and fits the quiet garden-house atmosphere · the BBQ grilling area at the resort is another option that groups of friends or families like to use in the evening, since you can buy ingredients and cook together in a relaxed setting, especially for groups renting a whole villa · for other meals, since the resort is in the Kung Wiman Beach area with seafood spots and local eateries scattered along the coastal road, many people choose to drive out for fresh seafood by the shore, which is part of the charm of visiting this side of Chanthaburi · the small mini-mart at the resort also helps when you want a snack or a late-night drink · overall the food here is simple but genuinely useful, suited to a style of stay that uses the resort as a base to head out and eat and explore, rather than expecting a fancy dining room at the resort.

Service — Service is the most consistently praised part of Forest Hill Resort · real reviews agree that the staff are friendly and attentive, take good care of guests, and what many people are impressed by is that the team helps recommend places to visit nearby — viewpoints, beaches, and local eateries — which makes planning easier for first-time visitors to Chanthaburi · being a small resort, the care comes across as warm and homey in a garden-house way, not the formal service of a big hotel · there's a 24-hour front desk, so guests arriving late or needing help can still reach someone · one thing to understand, by the nature of a small place, is that staff numbers are limited, so when the resort is full or several large groups are in at once, some services may take a little waiting, which is normal for this kind of resort · overall, service is a strength and a reason many reviews give high marks for the impression it leaves.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — Gathered from reviews on booking platforms like Trip.com and Agoda and local review sites; while the number of reviews is still modest because it's a small place, the picture is fairly consistent and comes out positive · on the praise side: a quiet atmosphere in nature, clean rooms and houses, a location close to Kung Wiman Beach just a few minutes' drive away, convenient and spacious parking, good-quality food, friendly staff who help recommend places to visit, and the privacy of the villas with private pools · many say it's great for an unhurried stay and for travelling in a group · on the watch-out side: the thing to understand is that the resort isn't on the beach — you have to drive about 1–1.6 km to the shore — so anyone expecting to walk straight down to the water may need to adjust their expectations · next is that it's a small place where facilities aren't as complete as a big hotel, with no fitness centre or spa, and getting around is easiest with your own car · on top of that, the still-modest number of reviews means the score can swing with each period's experience, so anyone who wants certainty should ask the resort directly about room and service details before booking.

"We came as a group and rented a villa with a private pool — so much fun, the kids got to swim right at the house. Rooms were clean and quiet. The only gripe is you need a car; without one it's a bit of a hassle getting around."

Price comparison and value — Room rates at Forest Hill Resort start at around THB 1,500/night for an entry room, climbing to about THB 6,000/night or more for a large villa with a private pool or the house for a group of 8, with breakfast already included · compared with pool villas in the main tourist towns like Hua Hin or Khao Yai, where private villas usually start much higher, this place counts as good value among reachable private-pool villa stays, especially when split among several people in a group or family, which brings the per-person cost down a lot · what adds to the value is the free parking, included breakfast, and pet policy, which save both money and worry for people bringing dogs and cats along · if you're planning a trip to the Kung Wiman Beach side of Chanthaburi with a car, travelling in numbers, and you weigh quiet and privacy over a beachfront location, the money you spend here comes back well · but if the weight of your trip is on staying right by the sea with the beach a step away, you may want to compare it with beachfront resorts in the same area before deciding.

Good to know before booking — There are a few things that make the stay smoother · one, you should have your own car, because the resort is out of town in a garden area near the beach, and public transport isn't as convenient as in town; a car lets you get around Kung Wiman Beach, the viewpoints, and the town of Chanthaburi with ease · two, if you're coming specifically for a villa with a private pool, specify the room type clearly when booking, because each house is different and stock is limited · three, if you're bringing a pet, let the resort know and ask about the charge and conditions ahead of time · four, over long holidays and Chanthaburi's tourist season (late rainy into early cool season and the fruit season), stays in this area fill quickly, so book ahead · five, since it's a small place with still-modest review numbers, we'd suggest contacting the resort directly to confirm prices, availability, and facilities before you travel, so it matches what you expect.

Summary — From all the real reviews, Forest Hill Resort Chanthaburi is the stay that best suits people who want to relax quietly in nature near Kung Wiman Beach, travelling in numbers or as a whole family, and want a villa with a private pool at a reachable price · the quiet, the privacy, the pet policy, the included breakfast, and the friendly staff make it a lovely choice for an unhurried getaway · but it's worth being clear with each other that this place is not a beachfront resort, and it's a small stay where facilities aren't as complete as a big hotel; having your own car makes the trip the most complete · if you're after a stay right by the sea with the beach a step away, or you want 4–5 star hotel service, you should consider a beachfront resort in the Chao Lao–Kung Wiman area instead · but for a family or group-of-friends trip where you want a private house in nature near the east-coast sea, on a sensible budget — Forest Hill Resort fits that need well.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Forest Hill Resort Chanthaburi

faq.q: Where is Forest Hill Resort · is it far from Kung Wiman Beach?
faq.a: The resort is in Sanam Chai subdistrict, Na Yai Am, Chanthaburi, in the Kung Wiman Beach area, reached via Highway 4036 · it's about 1–1.6 km from Kung Wiman Beach, just a few minutes' drive, but the resort itself is on the garden side, so it's quiet and not directly on the sea · near the Kung Wiman rock viewpoint and Wat Khao Sukim.

faq.q: Does Forest Hill Resort have villas with private pools?
faq.a: Yes · the resort has several house types, including villas with private pools, from a 3-bedroom layout sleeping 6 up to a house for 8, ideal for groups of friends and large families · there's also a shared outdoor pool · specify the room type clearly when booking, as stock is limited.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Forest Hill Resort · is breakfast included?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 1,500/night for an entry room, climbing to about THB 6,000+ for a villa with a private pool or the group house for 8 · breakfast is included in the room rate · very good value when travelling in numbers and splitting the cost.

faq.q: Does Forest Hill Resort allow pets?
faq.a: Yes · the resort welcomes pets (extra charge), a plus that isn't common at seaside resorts · we'd suggest letting the resort know and asking about the conditions in advance before you travel.

faq.q: Who is Forest Hill Resort for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for families travelling in numbers, groups of friends who want to rent a villa, couples after some privacy, and people bringing pets, in a quiet setting in nature near Kung Wiman Beach · if you're after a beachfront stay where you can walk straight to the sea, or 4–5 star hotel service, a beachfront resort in the Chao Lao–Kung Wiman area may suit you more.

faq.q: Can I stay at Forest Hill Resort without my own car?
faq.a: You can, but having your own car is the most convenient, because the resort is out of town in a garden area near the beach and public transport isn't as convenient as in a big city · without a car, plan your travel and the places you'll visit ahead, or ask the resort about transfer service.
